description: bqk-kos.org returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to a plain markdown-converting fetcher on https://bqk-kos.org/sistemet-e-pagesave/?lang=en, so no CBK page could be fetched directly in this pass; all candidate URLs come from search-index evidence rather than direct retrieval.

result.result_summary: 403 on first and only direct fetch attempt. Treated as bot-defended-but-live (search engines index the site heavily and PDFs are widely linked), NOT as dead.

why_it_matters: Collection design for this cell must assume a browser-grade fetcher with realistic headers, or PDF-first collection via direct wp-content/uploads links which appear to be served more permissively.

description: No machine-readable (HTML table, CSV, JSON or API) register of licensed payment institutions / e-money institutions was located. The licensed-institution register appears to be published only as a dated PDF snapshot.

result.result_summary: Only PDF editions found (e.g. Lista-e-institucioneve-financiare-22.04.2026-ALB.pdf).

why_it_matters: Enumerating the buyer universe requires PDF parsing and version diffing rather than an API pull; no stable per-institution identifier is guaranteed across editions.

description: Searching in Albanian for individual CBK licensing decisions (vendime licencimi) for payment institutions and e-money institutions in 2025-2026 returned mostly Bank of Albania material and CBK regulation texts, not a CBK archive of individual licensing/revocation decisions.

result.result_summary: No dedicated 'vendimet e Bordit / vendimet e licencimit' archive URL confirmed for BQK in this pass.

why_it_matters: Licence grants and revocations are the highest-value early signal of new market entrants; if no decisions archive exists, the dated register PDF diff plus press releases becomes the only detection mechanism.

description: Serbian-language searching confirmed the sr mirror (?lang=sr, /platni-sistem/) and Serbian annual reports, but no Serbian-language term for the CBK tender/procurement section was tested, and no Serbian-language edition of the licensed-institutions list was located.

result.result_summary: sr coverage confirmed for reports and payment-system pages only.

why_it_matters: Local-language coverage in sr is partial; procurement material may be Albanian-only, which affects any sr-only collection path.

description: Search indexes surfaced CBK content on non-canonical hosts: bqk.hpdevenv.com (statistics/time-series pages) and env2.bqk-kos.org (financial statements).

result.result_summary: Two apparent staging/mirror hosts indexed alongside production.

why_it_matters: A collector keyed on search results risks harvesting from a staging host whose content may be stale or may disappear; canonical bqk-kos.org paths must be resolved before scheduling collection.

description: The ECB MIP news item on the Western Balkans TIPS-clone project was surfaced only as a Romanian-language variant URL; the English variant used as the candidate URL is inferred by pattern, not observed.

result.result_summary: URL inferred from an observed language variant.

why_it_matters: Must be resolved by the deterministic liveness pass; do not treat the .en URL as confirmed.

description: Serbian-language (sr, Cyrillic) searching for Kosovo contract-award notices on payment/banking systems returned only Republic of Serbia procurement documents (mfin.gov.rs, prosveta.gov.rs, uap.gov.rs), not Kosovo ones. No Kosovo-specific sr-language procurement source was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Query 'Косово јавне набавке обавештење о додели уговора платни систем банкарски софтвер' surfaced zero Kosovo-domain results; all hits were Serbian state bodies.

why_it_matters: The e-Prokurimi portal exposes a Srpski interface, and Kosovo-Serb-majority municipalities are contracting authorities, so sr-language evidence almost certainly exists but is not reachable via generic Cyrillic web search — it must be pulled from inside the portal's sr locale. Without this, coverage of northern municipalities is at risk.

description: No dedicated procurement/tender page was found on trusti.org (Kosovo Pension Savings Fund) or for Posta e Kosoves in this pass, despite both being in the cell's named buyer list.

result.result_summary: sq searches returned corporate/press material and quarterly 'Trustorja' reports, not notice listings. Posta e Kosoves queries returned generic e-Prokurimi and municipality results.

why_it_matters: These are two of the most payments-relevant state buyers (pension disbursement; postal financial services and counter payments). Their notices must instead be reached via e-Prokurimi/OCDS filtered by buyer name, which adds a dependency on buyer-name normalisation.

description: A fetch of the e-Prokurimi homepage returned no explicit link to a public notice-search page; only links to KRPP, OSHP and AQP plus an economic-operator notice.

result.result_summary: Homepage acts as an informational shell; individual notices are reachable at deep SPIN_PROD DocumentManagement URLs found via search engines rather than via a discoverable search form.

why_it_matters: This is a hypothesis about site structure, not a verdict on availability — the search/browse function is likely behind a JS app or a login. Collection design should assume the OCDS API is the primary path and HTML is fallback.

description: No award notice naming the vendor(s) behind the eKosova card-payment gateway was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Searches confirmed eKosova accepts debit/credit card payments across banks and that ASHI operates it, but did not surface the acquiring/PSP contract or its winner.

why_it_matters: That contract is arguably the highest-signal single award in the cell — it identifies the acquirer/PSP trusted with government-wide card acceptance. It should be targeted directly in the OCDS pull with ASHI as buyer.

description: Serbian/Cyrillic searching for a Kosovo business register ('регистар привредних субјеката Косово') returns only Serbian APR, Republika Srpska bizreg and telecom-regulator registers — no Serbian-language interface to ARBK surfaced.

result.result_summary: No sr-language Kosovo company register located. ARBK appears to publish in sq and en; sr coverage of Kosovo entities appears to run through Serbian institutions instead.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language coverage of the Kosovo registry cell may be structurally unavailable; entities in Serb-majority municipalities may be registered in Serbia's APR rather than ARBK, creating a systematic blind spot in local presence mapping.

description: No public search interface for Kosovo's Register of Beneficial Owners (Law 08/L-265) was located in this pass — only the draft-consultation record and law text.

result.result_summary: UBO register legal basis confirmed; a live public UBO search URL was not found. Recorded as unverified, not absent.

why_it_matters: Beneficial ownership is the decisive field for distinguishing genuine vendor subsidiaries from local fronts; without the search endpoint, ownership analysis falls back on ARBK owner fields and OCCRP Aleph.

description: No official Kosovo government open-data dataset of ARBK records (e.g. a CKAN/open.data.rks-gov.net entry) was found; all bulk access appears to be via scraped third-party mirrors (arbk.org, ARBK Atlas, Open Data Kosovo, two APIs).

result.result_summary: Official bulk/machine-readable distribution of the registry not confirmed.

why_it_matters: Systematic monitoring must rely on unofficial mirrors of varying freshness and provenance, so every registry-derived claim needs verification against the official ARBK record.

description: Government guidance documents refer to ARBK's website as 'www.arbk.org', but arbk.org is in fact an independent open-data mirror while the official registrar is arbk.rks-gov.net.

result.result_summary: Naming collision between the official registrar domain and a third-party mirror observed in official-looking PDFs.

why_it_matters: Risk of misattributing third-party data to the official registrar; provenance must be recorded per record.

description: No Albanian-language Kosovo outlet was found that maintains a dedicated banking-technology or fintech beat/section. Coverage of vendors and core-banking/payments technology is incidental, scattered across generic 'ekonomi' sections, and largely triggered by press releases or scandals.

result.result_summary: Searched sq queries combining outlet names with digjitalizim/teknologji/softuer bankar; hits were either macro-economy pieces, PR product launches, or academic theses — no vertical tech-in-banking beat.

why_it_matters: Collection must be keyword/entity-driven across many outlets rather than feed-driven from one specialist source; expect low recall for quiet vendor deals that never produce a press release or a scandal.

description: No Kallxo/BIRN investigation specifically about a commercial bank's IT or software procurement surfaced in this pass. The closest hits were a Central Bank (BQK) tender-award investigation involving a businessman, telecom/IPKO transaction reporting, and generic procurement-management critiques.

result.result_summary: sq query 'Kallxo tender bankar kontratë softuer dyshime' returned police uniforms, e-scooters, bridges, air tickets, tax-certificate forgery — public-sector tenders, not bank IT contracts.

why_it_matters: Commercial banks in Kosovo are private entities not subject to the public procurement law, so their vendor contracts do not generate the tender paper trail investigative media feed on. Public-sector fintech exposure will surface mainly via BQK, ministries and public enterprises.

description: Serbian-language (sr) Kosovo media coverage of banking vendors/partnerships is thin. Kosovo Online and Gračanica-area outlets did not surface any bank-technology contract reporting; only KoSSev produced a relevant payments-digitalisation item.

result.result_summary: sr query on banke/ugovor/tender/softver returned mostly Wikipedia, a 2015 PAK contract-award PDF, and one KoSSev online-insurance item.

why_it_matters: sr-language coverage cannot be relied on as an independent confirmation channel for vendor/partnership events; it is better treated as a niche source for north-Kosovo payments and parallel-system issues.

description: The current business/economy section URL for Gazeta Express was not confirmed; the site-scoped query surfaced only its Media Ownership Monitor profile, not live section pages.

result.result_summary: No live gazetaexpress.com article URLs returned for the banking query.

why_it_matters: Could indicate a site restructure, indexing issue, or bot defences — not evidence the outlet is dead. Requires a direct fetch pass before being scheduled for collection.

description: A significant share of bank-related items on Indeksonline, Telegrafi and even Kallxo appear as sponsored content (Kallxo carries an explicit /artikull-i-sponsoruar/ namespace).

result.result_summary: Observed sponsored-article URL namespace on kallxo.com and PR-verbatim product pieces on indeksonline.net and telegrafi.com.

why_it_matters: Sponsored items are still useful as vendor/product disclosures but must never be scored as independent verification; the pipeline needs a sponsored-content flag derived from URL path and boilerplate.

description: No Serbian-language source was found that publishes a structured, machine-readable register of bank branches, ATMs or POS terminals operating in Serb-majority municipalities of Kosovo. Branch/ATM facts appear only as narrative statements inside news articles and government press releases.

result.result_summary: Only prose references (four prefabricated Poštanska štedionica ekspoziture at Jarinje, Brnjak, Končulj, Merdare; daily withdrawal cap reported as 10,000 RSD; ATMs reported non-functional) — no dataset.

why_it_matters: Any network-footprint or terminal-estate analysis for the parallel layer will have to be reconstructed manually from media text, with low precision and no update cadence.

description: The seed pointer 'kbs-ks.org' (implied Serbian-language Kosovo institutional site) produced no matching result in Serbian-language search; results redirected to kim.gov.rs, tanjug.rs and nbs.rs instead.

result.result_summary: Domain not confirmed to exist in this pass; not recorded as a source.

why_it_matters: Prevents fabricating an institutional source; the Kancelarija za KiM site (kim.gov.rs) appears to be the actual publisher of that material.

description: Searching eKapija specifically for Kosovo-related banking-software tenders returned only Serbia/regional vendor news (Asseco SEE, PEXIM); no eKapija tender notice referencing a Kosovo buyer or a Kosovo banking/payments procurement was located.

result.result_summary: eKapija is confirmed strong for regional vendor news, unconfirmed for Kosovo-specific tender coverage.

why_it_matters: Kosovo tender coverage must come from Kosovo's own e-procurement system, not from Serbian aggregators; do not over-weight eKapija for XK procurement.

description: No Albanian-language (sq) sources were pursued in this cell by design — the cell is the mandatory Serbian-language layer. Serbian-language sources dominated; English appeared only as secondary/wire material (globalsecurity.org mirror of RFE/RL).

result.result_summary: All 24 candidates are sr-primary; sq coverage is out of scope here and must come from the Albanian-language cells.

why_it_matters: Cross-language corroboration (CBK's Albanian statements vs NBS's Serbian statements) must be assembled at the run level, not inside this cell.

description: Access status for eKapija archive articles, ekapija-tenderi.com, and Politika was inferred from result snippets, not from a fetch. No liveness or paywall claim should be treated as verified.

result.result_summary: Marked as paywall/subscription 'suspected' or 'likely' rather than confirmed.

why_it_matters: Collection planning should budget for a possible subscription on eKapija tender content before assuming automated harvest is possible.

description: No standalone Kosovo banking/payments trade fair with a formal, published EXHIBITOR directory (booth list) was found. Kosovo events are conference-format with sponsor logo walls rather than expo-format with exhibitor catalogues; the nearest structured exhibitor directory is Serbian (Adria Media expo zone).

result.result_summary: sq queries using 'ekspozues', 'panair', 'stend' returned conference coverage, not exhibitor catalogues.

why_it_matters: Vendor rosters for Kosovo must be reconstructed from sponsor logos, speaker affiliations and award citations rather than harvested from a single exhibitor list — raises collection cost and lowers recall.

description: Serbian-language (sr) coverage of Kosovo-specific banking/fintech events was essentially absent. sr queries surfaced Serbia-proper association and expo sources (UBS-ASB, Adria Media), not Kosovo events; no sr-language conference agenda or sponsor roster for a Kosovo event was located.

result.result_summary: One sr query executed; all returns were Serbia-domestic. No Kosovo-hosted sr-language event source identified.

why_it_matters: The Serb-community banking segment in northern Kosovo and any sr-language forum activity remains an unmapped part of the partnership picture for this cell.

description: No national Kosovo ICT/banking AWARDS programme (an equivalent of e.g. 'ICT Awards' with published winner citations) was identified. Award signal for Kosovo banks comes exclusively from international publishers (Global Finance, Euromoney) and from the banks' own releases.

result.result_summary: sq award queries returned only Global Finance/Euromoney-derived coverage of BKT Kosova.

why_it_matters: Award-based case-study detail for Kosovo is limited to a handful of large banks; smaller banks' implementations are invisible through this channel.

description: Several candidate landing pages were identified from search-result metadata only and were not fetched in this pass: fintechkosovo.com, balkanfintechassociation.org, kosict.com sponsor page, ickosovo.com/events/all, ubs-asb.com/dogadjaji, and the Adria Media expo-zona enumeration.

result.result_summary: URLs recorded with reduced confidence_score; liveness and page structure not asserted.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must confirm these before they enter a collection schedule; a failure there should be treated as bot-defence or a moved path, not as a dead source.

description: The session's web-search budget (200 calls) was exhausted before planned follow-up queries on vendor-side sponsorship pages (Payten/Asseco SEE, Mellon, Visa/Mastercard Kosovo event sponsorships) and on Kosovo hackathon editions could be run.

result.result_summary: Final query on Payten/Asseco sponsorship returned a budget-exceeded notice; no results.

why_it_matters: The vendor-side mirror of the partnership map (vendor press pages announcing sponsorship of Kosovo/WB events) is unexplored and is likely the highest-yield remaining direction.

description: No evidence found of a live mobile-money / e-wallet product operated by either Kosovo mobile operator (Vala/Telekomi i Kosovës or IPKO) despite explicit sq-language searching for partnerships and new payment services.

result.result_summary: Searches returned operator corporate/product pages and market-structure articles only; no carrier-billing, wallet or mobile-money launch was surfaced.

why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumes telco mobile money is a growth vector. If no such product exists, the telco leg of the cell is about top-up distribution, billing systems and bill-pay acceptance rather than wallets — which changes which suppliers matter.

description: No public disclosure found of which acquirer/PSP serves the large retail chains (Viva Fresh, Meridian Express) or the fuel networks (HIB Petrol, Petrol Company) in Kosovo.

result.result_summary: Retailer sites confirm card acceptance and 'certified platforms' in generic terms; no bank or terminal-vendor partnership was named in any result.

why_it_matters: Merchant-acquirer linkage is the core competitive intelligence for the retail acceptance segment; it will have to be inferred from checkout-page inspection, terminal branding in store photos, or vendor case studies rather than from merchant announcements.

description: Hypothesised Kosovo payment-agent brand names 'PayLink' and 'SwiftPay' returned no Kosovo-specific results.

result.result_summary: Only Capital Ria, VllesaPagesa, Paysera Kosova and the Kos-Giro instrument were confirmed; the two guessed brands do not appear to exist in this market.

why_it_matters: Prevents a fabricated actor entering the actor map; the agent-network segment appears smaller and more concentrated than assumed.

description: Serbian-language (sr) searching for Kosovo adjacent-buyer payment actors returned mostly Serbia-proper sources (Pošta Srbije, Serbian insurers) rather than Kosovo-based Serbian-language sources; only the BQK sr-language card report was a true hit.

result.result_summary: One usable sr source found (BQK 'Korišćenje kartica na Kosovu'); Serbian-language Kosovo actors such as MTS d.o.o. Kosovo and northern-municipality utilities were not surfaced.

why_it_matters: The Serb-majority north has parallel payment habits and its own operators/billers; leaving it uncovered biases the acceptance picture toward the Albanian-language market.

description: The session's web-search budget (200 calls) was exhausted before planned queries on ARBK business registry, telco payment news monitoring, and MTS Kosovo could be executed.

result.result_summary: Two final planned queries returned a budget-exhausted notice instead of results.

why_it_matters: Coverage of the corporate-registry pointer and of Serbian-language telecom actors in this cell is incomplete and should be completed in a follow-up run.

description: Searched for Big Four (Deloitte/PwC/KPMG/EY) market studies with an explicit Kosovo banking or payments chapter. Deloitte's Digital Banking Maturity and CE Banking Outlook, and the CEE PSD2 surveys, were the only recurring products found, and none of the retrieved material evidenced Kosovo in the country sample.

result.result_summary: No Kosovo-specific Big Four banking market study located in this run; only regional CEE/SEE products whose Kosovo coverage is unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: If no Big Four Kosovo study exists, the consultancy/benchmark layer for this market rests on IFI reports (IMF/World Bank/EC) and local think tanks (Riinvest/GAP) instead — which changes both the evidence base and the credibility ceiling of any market sizing.

description: Albanian-phrase searching for 'Raporti i Auditorit të Pavarur' plus 'bankë' surfaced audited statements for NGOs, political entities, KOSTT, the Insurance Bureau, FINCA and the CBK — but no central index of commercial-bank audited statements, and nothing dated 2025.

result.result_summary: Bank external-audit reports exist but are scattered across individual bank websites with no aggregator; recent-year coverage was not reachable through general search.

why_it_matters: Collection must be per-bank (walk the CBK register of licensed banks and crawl each 'Raporte vjetore' section) rather than search-driven, and Wayback CDX will be needed for years whose PDFs were rotated off the live sites.

description: The session's web-search budget (200/200) was consumed before planned queries on EBRD/IFC Kosovo banking diagnostics, KPMG/EY Adriatic banking studies, ResearchGate/Google Scholar Albanian-language payment papers, and targeted Wayback recovery of specific vendor reference pages.

result.result_summary: Several intended query lines could not be executed; the cell is well covered on IFI, audit, think-tank and archive layers but thin on EBRD/IFC and on named-vendor archive recovery.

why_it_matters: Coverage of this cell is incomplete in a known, specific way; a follow-up run with fresh budget should start from the listed unexecuted queries rather than repeating what is already covered here.

description: Serbian-language searching for Kosovo banking-sector research returned CBK's own sr-language mirror, a SCIndeks article, and Serbian e-banking studies about Serbia — but no Serbian-language Kosovo-focused think tank or consultancy producing banking/payments analysis.

result.result_summary: The sr-language analyst layer for Kosovo appears to be effectively absent; sr coverage rests on the CBK mirror and Serbian academic indexes.

why_it_matters: Any claim of balanced sq/sr source coverage must acknowledge that the sr side is institutional/academic only, with no independent sr analyst voice located.

description: Serbian/Cyrillic search for Kosovo donor procurement in banking/payments returned only Serbia-domestic World Bank and NBS material, no Kosovo-specific donor procurement source.

result.result_summary: Query "Косово тендер набавка банкарски систем плаћања ЕБРД Светска банка пројекат" surfaced mre.gov.rs, minrzs.gov.rs, mfin.gov.rs and nbs.rs documents about Serbian projects; nothing about Kosovo (XK) donor-financed financial-sector procurement.

why_it_matters: Confirms that for this cell the Serbian-language layer is not a productive discovery channel: IFI/EU procurement for Kosovo is published in English, and the local mirror is Albanian. Serbian-language coverage will need to come from Kosovo-institution sr-language versions rather than from open Cyrillic web search.

description: No Serbian-language equivalents of Kosovo donor-procurement terminology could be attached to any candidate in this slice.

result.result_summary: Every candidate discovered carries either English (IFI/EU) or Albanian (BQK, e-Prokurimi) terminology. Serbian-language terms such as 'обавештење о додели уговора' / 'javna nabavka' did not lead to Kosovo donor-financed financial-sector sources in this pass.

why_it_matters: Mandatory local-language coverage is only half satisfied (sq yes, sr no). A follow-up pass should test the Serbian-language versions of Kosovo institutional sites directly rather than via search engines.

description: No dedicated MCC (Millennium Challenge Corporation) Kosovo financial-sector or payments procurement source was found.

result.result_summary: Searches confirm Kosovo is among the countries implementing an MCC compact, but no compact procurement notice or TOR touching banking/payments surfaced. MCC Kosovo work appears energy- and governance-focused.

why_it_matters: MCC can be deprioritised for this cell unless a later compact component adds digital financial services; avoids wasting collector budget on a dry channel.

description: KfW has no discoverable Kosovo-specific tender/procurement listing for its financial-sector programmes.

result.result_summary: KfW appears in results as a funder of the Kosovo Credit Guarantee Fund (KCGF) and of financial-sector grant/lending operations, but its consultant procurement for Kosovo was not locatable via open search in this pass.

why_it_matters: KfW-funded vendor engagement in Kosovo will likely have to be inferred indirectly from KCGF publications and from KfW ex-post evaluation reports rather than from a tender feed.

description: EBRD's live procurement notice detail appears to sit behind ECEPP/SMART-by-GEP registration.

result.result_summary: Search summaries state registration is required to view current procurement notices. Not independently fetched, so this is a hypothesis about access, not a verified verdict.

why_it_matters: If confirmed, EBRD notice text needs an authenticated or manual collection tier, while EBRD PSD/TCPSD pages remain the open substitute.

description: Serbian-language (sr) searching for Kosovo bank announcements returned no Kosovo bank sources at all.

result.result_summary: The query 'banke na Kosovu saopštenje mobilno bankarstvo nova platforma' returned only Serbian, Bosnian and Croatian bank sites (Erste RS, Nova Banka BiH, Banca Intesa, Addiko) — nothing from any Kosovo-licensed private bank.

why_it_matters: Suggests the private commercial banks in Kosovo do not maintain Serbian-language newsrooms, so sr-language monitoring of this cell is likely low-yield and effort should be concentrated on sq and en. This should be re-tested with bank-specific sr terms before being treated as settled.

description: TEB Sh.A. Kosovo appears to have no conventional press-release archive.

result.result_summary: Generic sq querying for 'TEB ... lajme njoftime raporte vjetore' returned only Kosovo news portals (Telegrafi, Bota Sot, Kosova Sot) and no TEB pages; a domain-scoped query surfaced only About Us, Digital Banking Channels and an 'Important Notice' page on teb-kos.com.

why_it_matters: For TEB the collection design must lean on page-diffing of notices/product pages plus BNP Paribas / TEB Group parent disclosure, rather than a newsroom feed.

description: No public announcement of a core-banking or payment-platform vendor selection by any Kosovo private bank was found in this run.

result.result_summary: An en query pairing the banks with Visa/Mastercard/core-banking vendor terms returned only an EBRD facility, a ProCredit Visa B2B award and a Kosovo Banking Association payments forum — no named platform vendor.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: vendor spend is not announced directly. Detection must come from indirect tells (app store developer/rebrand signals, forum speaker lists, parent-group IT chapters, migration notices), which is how the candidate mix above is weighted.

description: Direct fetch of the BKT Kosova root domain failed on TLS.

result.result_summary: WebFetch of https://www.bkt-ks.com/ returned 'unable to verify the first certificate'. The domain is well indexed and multiple deep pages appear in search results, so this is a hypothesis about the cert chain / a WAF, not evidence the site is dead.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should use a client tolerant of an incomplete chain and try the apex without www before marking any BKT URL unreachable.

description: Every direct fetch of bankassoc-kos.com (homepage, /about-us/member-banks/, /events/payment-forum-2/) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden, as did amik.org/Anetaret-e-AMIK.

result.result_summary: Four 403s across the two most important association domains in this cell. Both domains are well indexed by search engines, so the sites are almost certainly live and merely WAF/bot-defended. Recorded as UNVERIFIED, not dead.

why_it_matters: The two canonical membership rosters for banks and MFIs cannot be collected by plain HTTP. Collection design must assume browser-based fetching for this cell, or reconstruct rosters from member-side and regulator-side sources.

description: Two search-indexed deep URLs 404'd on fetch: https://kosict.com/sponsors-partners/ and https://oegjk.org/anetaresia/al-lista-e-anetareve/lista-e-plote/.

result.result_summary: Both are sponsor/member-roster pages — the highest-value targets on their sites. 404 pattern suggests site restructuring or per-edition URL rotation rather than removal.

why_it_matters: Sponsor lists are edition-scoped and disappear; without Wayback capture the multi-year vendor-sponsorship time series is lost. Collection should snapshot these aggressively and back-fill from web archives.

description: No official, independent website was located for the Kosovo insurance association (Shoqata e Sigurimeve të Kosovës) despite Albanian-language searching.

result.result_summary: The association exists (founded 2002, ~14 member insurers per press coverage; has a YouTube channel and a D&B business-directory entry) but no association-owned member directory URL was found in this run.

why_it_matters: The insurance leg of this cell is currently served only by third-party stubs and by the statutory motor bureau (BKS). The authoritative insurer roster will likely have to come from the CBK licensed-institutions register instead of an association directory.

description: Serbian-language searching for Kosovo industry bodies returned almost no Kosovo-specific results.

result.result_summary: The query 'Udruženje banaka Kosova članovi banke' was dominated by Udruženje banaka Srbije (Serbia). The only genuine sr-language Kosovo hit was the BQK ?lang=sr newsroom. No Kosovo industry association appears to publish a Serbian-language member directory.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language coverage of this cell is structurally thin, not merely under-searched — Kosovo's associations publish in sq and en. Serbian-language monitoring should be redirected to regulator locale pages and to north-Kosovo/Serbia-facing business media rather than to association sites. There is also a strong false-positive risk of Serbia's UBS being mistaken for a Kosovo body.

description: Oda Ekonomike e Kosovës (KCC/OEK) claims 30 sectoral associations and 15,000+ members but no online searchable member registry was located.

result.result_summary: Site navigation exposes departments, regional units, services and regulations, but no public member-lookup endpoint surfaced in search.

why_it_matters: The statutory chamber is a broad pointer in principle but appears unusable as a structured roster; do not budget collection effort against it until an actual registry endpoint is confirmed.

description: Named KosICT sponsors recovered (Paysera as Platinum, ProCredit Bank Kosova as General sponsor, IDS Consulting as Gold) come from earlier festival editions, not confirmed 2025.

result.result_summary: The 2025 edition's figures were recoverable (2,798 participants, 208 companies, 47 speakers, 40 exhibitors) but its sponsor roster was not.

why_it_matters: Vendor-sponsorship claims must be edition-dated or they mislead. Any downstream analysis must carry the edition year with each sponsor fact.

description: WebFetch of the BQK licensing page (https://bqk-kos.org/mbikeqyrja-financiare/licencimi-i-institucioneve-financiare/?lang=en) returned HTTP 403.

result.result_summary: 403 Forbidden on the regulator's own licensing section, while the same domain's PDFs and news URLs are indexed by search engines. Read as bot-defended-but-live, not dead. Not verified either way.

why_it_matters: The BQK site is the backbone of this cell; the collector must use browser-grade headers or a headless browser rather than a plain HTTP client, or the highest-value register will silently fail to collect.

description: No separate, standalone BQK web register specifically for payment institutions and e-money institutions was located — PIs/EMIs appear to be listed inside the general dated 'Lista e institucioneve financiare' PDF alongside banks and MFIs.

result.result_summary: Searches in sq for a distinct PI/EMI registry returned only the combined list PDF and licensing manuals.

why_it_matters: Actor extraction for the payments layer requires PDF table parsing plus category filtering, not a clean structured feed; and licence-event detection depends on diffing PDF editions.

description: Serbian-language (sr) searching surfaced almost no Kosovo-specific payments sources; results skewed to Serbia-proper providers (PaySpot, TransferNova, Pošta Srbije PostKeš).

result.result_summary: The only genuinely Kosovo-relevant sr-language asset found was the Serbian locale of the FIKS cluster site (fintechkosovo.com/home-srb) and the sr locale of Raiffeisen Kosovo.

why_it_matters: Payments coverage for Serb-majority municipalities (north Kosovo, Gračanica, Štrpce) — where dinar-cash and parallel remittance channels matter — is a real blind spot that sr-language searching on generic terms will not close.

description: Aggregator-sourced Kosovo fintech funding figures (e.g. a '$15M digital banking round') came from a low-authority blog rather than a primary source, and no matching company was named.

result.result_summary: Could not corroborate any specific Kosovo payments funding round against a company announcement or a reputable database within this pass.

why_it_matters: Funding-signal sources for this market are thin and partly synthetic; the pipeline must require primary corroboration before recording a funding event.

description: The canonical corporate domain for OneFor was inferred (onefor.com) rather than reached; coverage of the Kosovo launch was found only via media syndications.

result.result_summary: No direct fetch of a OneFor Kosovo corporate page was performed in this pass.

why_it_matters: A key licensed wallet actor currently has only a hypothesised primary URL; the verification pass must resolve it before the source is trusted.

description: No established Albanian-language term was found in circulation for 'e-money institution' distinct from the generic 'institucion financiar jobankar (IFJB)'; local coverage describes EMIs simply as IFJB or by the English 'EMI'.

result.result_summary: sq queries for an EMI-specific phrase returned only IFJB and generic 'shërbime pagesash' phrasing.

why_it_matters: Query design must not assume a distinct sq EMI term; searching on IFJB + brand names is the reliable path, otherwise EMI licence events will be missed in local-language monitoring.

description: No Kosovo-specific Visa or Mastercard press release was located on either scheme's own newsroom. Searches surfaced only region-wide CEMEA/SEE items (stablecoin initiatives, 'Agentic Ready') with no XK naming.

result.result_summary: Scheme-operator primary announcements naming Kosovo appear to be rare or absent publicly; Kosovo scheme events reach the public mainly via issuers, BQK and local media.

why_it_matters: Means the cell cannot rely on scheme newsrooms as the primary trigger for XK rollout signals; issuer + regulator + local press must carry that load.

description: No public evidence was found identifying the third-party card processor(s) or ATM/POS managed-service providers actually contracted by Kosovo banks. Payten/ASEE publishes regional aggregate figures but no Kosovo client references were surfaced; Printec, BPC, NCR/Diebold Nixdorf returned no Kosovo-specific results.

result.result_summary: Processor and self-service vendor attribution for XK is not publicly documented in search-reachable sources.

why_it_matters: Vendor-displacement analysis for the XK estate will require indirect inference (procurement notices, job ads, ATM screen/branding photos, certification lists) rather than direct vendor disclosure.

description: No dedicated ATM-outsourcing or independent ATM deployer (IAD) operating in Kosovo was identified in sq, sr or en searches; sq terms used included 'bankomat', 'rrjeti i bankomatëve', 'shërbimi i bankomatëve'.

result.result_summary: Kosovo appears to have no visible non-bank ATM deployer market, unlike several neighbouring markets.

why_it_matters: Suggests ATM estate change in XK is driven entirely by bank-side decisions, so bank procurement and bank reporting are the only viable observation points.

description: Searching e-prokurimi for ATM/POS-specific contract notices via general web search did not return XK payment-hardware awards; the portal's content is largely behind its own search UI and per-document ASP.NET IDs.

result.result_summary: Procurement evidence exists but is not reachable by ordinary web search; requires in-portal querying.

why_it_matters: Collection design must include an in-portal search routine rather than relying on search-engine indexing.

description: No vendor case study, press release or customer page was found in which a global core-banking vendor (Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Finastra/Misys, TCS BaNCS, Infosys Finacle) explicitly names a Kosovo bank as a customer.

result.result_summary: Searches for core-banking go-lives returned only unrelated markets (Malawi, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Kenya) and generic vendor-comparison listicles. The only attribution of Temenos T24 to a Kosovo bank (Raiffeisen Bank Kosova) comes from a paid technographics aggregator, not from the vendor.

why_it_matters: The core-banking layer, the most strategically important, is precisely where vendor-side disclosure for Kosovo is weakest. Installed-base mapping for core will need bank-side and regulator-side evidence (annual reports, procurement notices, job ads naming platforms) rather than vendor pointers.

description: Halcom's public 'banks using Halcom' list, fetched directly, covers Serbia, Slovenia, Bosnia-Herzegovina and Albania and names no Kosovo bank, despite secondary search snippets suggesting Halcom entered the Kosovo market and that Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo was an early Halcom mobile-bank user.

result.result_summary: Fetched list contains four country groupings, none of them Kosovo. The Kosovo market-entry claim could not be corroborated on a primary vendor page in this pass.

why_it_matters: Illustrates that vendor customer lists in this region are maintained per legal entity and can silently drop or never include Kosovo; absence from a logo wall must not be read as absence from the market. Archived snapshots are needed.

description: Serbian-language searching for vendor references to Kosovo banks produced essentially no vendor-side material.

result.result_summary: The sr query on banking software suppliers/references returned only Wikipedia entries and Central Bank of Kosovo payment-system documents, no vendor customer pages.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language vendor communication about Kosovo appears to be effectively absent, probably for political/market reasons: regional vendors address the Kosovo market in Albanian or English. Serbian remains useful for Serbia-headquartered vendors' general reference lists (Comtrade, Asseco SEE Serbia, Halcom) but not as a Kosovo-specific channel.

description: No vendor reference naming a Kosovo institution was found for AML/financial-crime software or for e-signature/PKI/trust services.

result.result_summary: AML searches returned only global vendor listicles (NICE Actimize, Oracle, ComplyAdvantage, Ondato) with no Kosovo customer. No qualified trust-service-provider or e-signature vendor case study naming a Kosovo bank was located.

why_it_matters: Two of the six product categories in this cell's scope currently have zero vendor-side evidence, so the installed-base picture would be badly skewed toward ATM/POS and digital banking if built from pointers alone.

description: The FinTech Futures Kosovo tag page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch.

result.result_summary: 403 Forbidden on https://www.fintechfutures.com/us/tag/kosovo/ ; individual article URLs surfaced normally through search, so the site is judged bot-defended-but-live, not dead.

why_it_matters: The single best country-indexed trade-press stream for this cell needs a browser-grade collection method; a naive HTTP collector would silently record zero Kosovo deals.

description: AppsRunTheWorld technographics profiles for Raiffeisen Bank Kosova and ProCredit Bank Kosovo exist but expose only teaser fields.

result.result_summary: Vendor attributions (e.g. Temenos T24 at Raiffeisen Bank Kosova) appear in snippets; the sourced detail sits behind subscription.

why_it_matters: The most complete Kosovo bank technology-stack index found is commercial and uncorroborated, so it can seed hypotheses but cannot be used as evidence without licensing or independent confirmation.

description: Neither ASEE nor Payten surfaced a publicly named Kosovo bank customer in searchable news, despite ASEE operating a registered Prishtina entity (Asseco SEE sh.p.k.) and listing a Prishtina office.

result.result_summary: Kosovo presence is confirmed at entity level only; deal-level references remain unattributed and would need reverse-lookup from the bank side or from procurement/registry data.

why_it_matters: The incumbent-to-displace in Kosovo is likely ASEE/Payten, but without a named reference the competitive claim cannot be evidenced from vendor marketing alone.

description: Serbian-language searching for banking-software integrators with Kosovo references returned only generic banking-sector and encyclopaedic results, no integrator reference lists.

result.result_summary: Query 'integrator bankarski softver Srbija Kosovo reference banke' produced Wikipedia, a university course PDF on core banking, and unrelated AI-software marketing.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language vendor references to Kosovo are likely suppressed or phrased around 'region'/'Zapadni Balkan' rather than 'Kosovo' for political reasons; the search vocabulary must be adjusted rather than concluding no coverage exists.

description: No Serbian-language ('sr') vendor site for a Kosovo-serving integrator was located in this pass; sr coverage came only via Halcom's sr locale and Saga's Serbian-market coverage in English trade press.

result.result_summary: sr-language search executed and documented, but yielded no sr-native primary vendor source specific to the Kosovo territory.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language sources are needed to cover the Serbian-owned banking footprint and the northern-Kosovo market segment; the gap is a coverage weakness, not evidence of absence.

description: No evidence surfaced linking Turkish payments/banking-technology vendors (Provus, Kartek, Fineksus and peers) to Kosovo bank implementations, despite Turkish-owned banking presence in Kosovo (TEB, BKT-linked activity).

result.result_summary: Searches returned only Provus's Romanian RomCard acquisition and general Kosovo banking-sector background.

why_it_matters: Turkish bank ownership in Kosovo is a plausible channel for Turkish vendors, so absence of evidence here is most likely a language gap (Turkish-language search not performed) rather than genuine absence.

description: Croatian and Slovenian integrators other than Halcom/Bankart (e.g. Combis, Mstart, Span, Ericsson Nikola Tesla) produced no Kosovo banking references in this pass.

result.result_summary: A combined query naming Combis and Mstart alongside Kosovo returned no matching results.

why_it_matters: The Croatia/Slovenia leg of the regional channel is under-evidenced; these firms typically serve Kosovo indirectly via group banks (NLB, Erste, Raiffeisen) and may only be visible through group-level IT sourcing.

description: The STIKK member directory was fetched successfully but presents members by sponsorship tier without visible filtering or a sector facet, and only two members read as explicitly fintech.

result.result_summary: Approximately 60+ members listed; banking/fintech identification requires opening each member profile.

why_it_matters: Enumerating the Kosovo-registered arms of regional integrators from this directory will require full-profile crawling rather than a filtered query.

description: Searching for live Kosovo job ads that explicitly name core banking products (Temenos T24, Oracle Flexcube) returned only non-Kosovo postings (US/Middle East aggregators) plus one technographics profile.

result.result_summary: No indexed Kosovo-located job ad naming a specific core banking product was retrievable through general web search.

why_it_matters: Platform names in Kosovo ads are likely present but not surfaced by general search engines because local boards render postings dynamically and delete them after the deadline. Collection must be on-board and continuous rather than retrospective via search.

description: The 'portalpune' brand resolves to two distinct sites — portalpune.com (Kosovo) and portalpune.al (Albania) — and search results conflate them; boilerplate 'market leader since 2008' text also appears in scraped-looking copy.

result.result_summary: Both domains exist and serve job listings; the Kosovo-relevant one is portalpune.com.

why_it_matters: A collector configured on the wrong domain would silently gather Albanian rather than Kosovar vacancies, corrupting a market-level hiring signal.

description: No stable Albanian-language term for 'core banking system' emerged from search; local ads appear to use either the English phrase or loose descriptions ('sistemi bankar', 'sistemet e IT-së').

result.result_summary: Glossary gap: 'sistemi bazë bankare' is a constructed rather than attested term, and 'sistemi bankar' is noisy (it commonly means the banking sector as a whole, not the software).

why_it_matters: Keyword rules built on 'sistemi bankar' will produce heavy false positives; matching should rely on English product names embedded in sq text plus role titles.

description: LinkedIn job and profile search — the single highest-yield surface for platform-name leakage — is behind an auth wall and its ToS forbids automated collection.

result.result_summary: Only public company pages were reachable; no jobs listing content retrievable.

why_it_matters: The richest signal in this cell cannot be automated; it needs an analyst seat or a licensed provider, which is a budget/process decision rather than an engineering one.

description: No Kosovo-specific hiring or presence footprint was found for Halcom or Printec in this pass, despite both being regional payments/e-banking vendors.

result.result_summary: Search surfaced Asseco SEE (Prishtina banking unit) and Comtrade Computers (bank clients listed via STIKK) but nothing Kosovo-located for Halcom or Printec.

why_it_matters: Absence here is weak evidence only — these vendors may serve Kosovo from Ljubljana/Athens/Belgrade with no local hiring, so their footprint must be sought in tender records and partner directories instead of job boards.
